data.title: Information panels at Prosné – Zlatý kôň and Uhliská
data.excerpt: On 5 April 2014 our civic association Hradiská put up two information panels above Prosné: one at the Zlatý kôň small fort of the Púchov culture, the other at the Uhliská sacrificial site. Archaeologists, the discoverers of both sites and the Celts of the Vae Victis association came to support the event, and the village of Udiča paid for the panels.
data.metaTitle: Information panels at Prosné – Zlatý kôň and Uhliská

children.text: On 5 April 2014 our civic association Hradiská, together with Mr Štefan Žilovec
organised the installation of information panels at
the Zlatý kôň small fort of the Púchov culture
the Uhliská sacrificial site of the Púchov culture.

Our initial fears about how the weather would turn out fortunately came to nothing (the god Taranis evidently reconsidered his original plans in view of the importance of our event) and we had pleasant weather all day.

Several distinguished guests came to the site to support us: the discoverer of the Zlatý kôň small fort, Mr Štefan Meliš, together with almost all the members of the archaeology club in Považská Bystrica (Messrs Olšovský, Zemančík, Janech, Miko), the archaeologist Jozef Moravčík, who led the club in the past, the archaeologist of the Považie Museum in Žilina Andrea Slaná, the archaeologist of the Regional Monuments Board in Žilina Katarína Vlaszatá, the archaeologist Peter Schreiber, the discoverer of the sacrificial site Mr Kondrčík and, not least, the Celts from Havránok – the Vae Victis association – and many other interesting guests. For the first time our panel installation did not escape the representatives of the media either.

blocks.alt: The marked spot where we put the panel

children.text: The first one we put up was the information panel below the Zlatý kôň hillfort. Our co-organiser Mr Štefan Žilovec helped us out not only by obtaining the necessary consents from the landowners, but also by creating (clearing) the spot where we put the panel up, and by providing a lorry that carried both panels out into terrain that is hard to reach.

On the spot itself our lads knew exactly what to do, so the panel was in place within a few minutes. At its unveiling, the discoverer of the small fort, Štefan Meliš, first told us how he had managed to find it, and we learnt several legends connected with the small fort from him. Then the archaeologist Jozef Moravčík gave us an expert account of the most interesting finds from the small fort and told us about the Púchov culture.
 
 We then wanted to proceed to the unveiling of the panel itself, when Mr Stanislav Miko asked to speak; on behalf of the archaeology club in Považská Bystrica and the civic association Pamäť a úcta he presented our association with a certificate of recognition for our work. He said, among other things, that they regard us as worthy successors in the work of the archaeology club. Mr Miko's words and the certificate of recognition handed to us pleased us greatly and at the same time encouraged us in our further work. Thank you.
 
 Then came the “blessing” of the panel itself, performed by Čendo Žrec with good mead, and its unveiling.

blocks.alt: The lads from the Hradiská association putting up the panel

children.text: After looking round the Zlatý kôň small fort we gradually moved on to the Uhliská sacrificial site.

At the sacrificial site of the Púchov culture at Uhliská we were awaited not only by the Celts of the Vae Victis association, who had come in full Celtic equipment, with shields and weapons, but also by Mr Ladislav Janech, who had prepared at the sacrificial site a valuable little exhibition of interesting finds of the Púchov culture which he keeps in his museum. Visitors could thus not only see with their own eyes the precious finds left in the territory of present-day Slovakia by the people of the Púchov culture more than 2,000 years ago, but also touch them. Its discoverer, Mr Peter Kondrčík, also came to the sacrificial site and told us how he had managed to discover it, and he recalled as well a letter sent to him by Anton Petrovský-Šichman, in which he wrote that this place would be of exceptional archaeological importance in the future. Mr Jozef Moravčík again gave us a sound account of the course of the excavation and of the finds made at the sacrificial site. In addition, the Celtic druid Brendyx told us something about the way the Celts carried out human sacrifices in the past, and then consecrated the panel in the name of the Celtic sun god Taranis.

children.text: The whole day passed in a very pleasant, friendly atmosphere and without any great stress. We thank everyone who took part in organising this splendid event, and we also thank the people from the surrounding area who came to support us for the good turnout.

Finally, let me add that the cost of each panel, 150 euros, which practically corresponds to the production costs of making it and from which our association derives no profit at all, will be paid for us by the village of Udiča on the promise of its mayor, Mr Jozef Slámka, for which it deserves great thanks.
